entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical vision-language framework for automated histopathology report generation using the UNI foundation model with multi-resolution pyramidal patch selection from whole slide images.

entry.title: Hardware-accelerated graph neural networks: an alternative approach for neuromorphic event-based audio classification and keyword spotting on SoC FPGA

author.name: Kamil Jeziorek, Piotr Wzorek, Krzysztof Blachut, Hiroshi Nakano, Manon Dampfhoffer, Thomas Mesquida, Hiroaki Nishi, Thomas Dalgaty, Tomasz Kryjak

entry.summary: Presents an FPGA implementation of event-graph neural networks for neuromorphic audio processing, achieving competitive accuracy with 10x fewer parameters than state-of-the-art.

entry.title: Memes-as-Replies: Can Models Select Humorous Manga Panel Responses?

author.name: Ryosuke Kohita, Seiichiro Yoshioka

entry.summary: Introduces the Meme Reply Selection task with MaMe-Re, a benchmark of 100K human-annotated manga panel-social media post pairs, testing whether LLMs can select humorous meme responses.

entry.title: Muon with Spectral Guidance: Efficient Optimization for Scientific Machine Learning

author.name: Binghang Lu, Jiahao Zhang, Guang Lin

entry.summary: Proposes SpecMuon, a spectral-aware optimizer that combines the Muon optimizer's orthogonalized geometry with a mode-wise relaxed scalar auxiliary variable mechanism for physics-informed neural networks and neural operators.

entry.title: ModalImmune: Immunity Driven Unlearning via Self Destructive Training

author.name: Rong Fu, Jia Yee Tan, Wenxin Zhang, Zijian Zhang, Ziming Wang, Zhaolu Kang, Muge Qi, Shuning Zhang, Simon Fong

entry.summary: Presents ModalImmune, a training framework that enforces modality immunity by intentionally collapsing selected modality information during training, making multimodal models robust to missing input channels at deployment.

entry.title: Online Prediction of Stochastic Sequences with High Probability Regret Bounds

author.name: Matthias Frey, Jonathan H. Manton, Jingge Zhu

entry.summary: Presents high-probability regret bounds for universal prediction of stochastic sequences, complementing existing bounds that hold only in expectation. Shows O(T^{-1/2} δ^{-1/2}) convergence rate.

entry.title: Robust Stochastic Gradient Posterior Sampling with Lattice Based Discretisation

author.name: Zier Mensch, Lars Holdijk, Samuel Duffield, Maxwell Aifer, Patrick J. Coles, Max Welling, Miranda C. N. Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes Stochastic Gradient Lattice Random Walk (SGLRW), an SGLD variant that introduces noise only through off-diagonal covariance elements, yielding greater robustness to minibatch size while maintaining asymptotic correctness.

entry.title: Exploring New Frontiers in Vertical Federated Learning: the Role of Saddle Point Reformulation

author.name: Aleksandr Beznosikov, Georgiy Kormakov, Alexander Grigorievskiy, Mikhail Rudakov, Ruslan Nazykov, Alexander Rogozin, Anton Vakhrushev, Andrey Savchenko, Martin Tak\'a\v{c}, Alexander Gasnikov

entry.summary: Explores saddle point reformulation of Vertical Federated Learning via Lagrangian functions, enabling stochastic modifications including compression, partial participation, and coordinate selection for practical VFL scenarios.

entry.title: Local adapt-then-combine algorithms for distributed nonsmooth optimization: Achieving provable communication acceleration

author.name: Luyao Guo, Xinli Shi, Wenying Xu, Jinde Cao

entry.summary: Proposes FlexATC, a communication-efficient distributed optimization framework using probabilistic local updates for composite optimization over networks. Achieves provable communication acceleration with convergence rates decoupled from network topology.

entry.title: Multi-Channel Replay Speech Detection using Acoustic Maps

author.name: Michael Neri, Tuomas Virtanen

entry.summary: Proposes acoustic maps as spatial features for multi-channel replay speech detection, using beamforming-derived directional energy distributions. Achieves competitive performance with only ~6k parameters.

entry.title: Utility-Preserving De-Identification for Math Tutoring: Investigating Numeric Ambiguity in the MathEd-PII Benchmark Dataset

author.name: Zhuqian Zhou, Kirk Vanacore, Bakhtawar Ahtisham, Jinsook Lee, Doug Pietrzak, Daryl Hedley, Jorge Dias, Chris Shaw, Ruth Sch\"afer, Ren\'e F. Kizilcec

entry.summary: Investigates numeric ambiguity in PII detection for math tutoring transcripts, introducing MathEd-PII benchmark. Addresses the problem of over-redacting mathematical content that resembles personal identifiers.

entry.title: Detecting Deepfakes with Multivariate Soft Blending and CLIP-based Image-Text Alignment

author.name: Jingwei Li, Jiaxin Tong, Pengfei Wu

entry.summary: Proposes MSBA-CLIP for deepfake detection, using multivariate soft blending augmentation with CLIP-guided forgery intensity estimation to improve generalization across diverse forgery techniques.

entry.title: DressWild: Feed-Forward Pose-Agnostic Garment Sewing Pattern Generation from In-the-Wild Images

author.name: Zeng Tao, Ying Jiang, Yunuo Chen, Tianyi Xie, Huamin Wang, Yingnian Wu, Yin Yang, Abishek Sampath Kumar, Kenji Tashiro, Chenfanfu Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes DressWild, a feed-forward pipeline that reconstructs physics-consistent 2D sewing patterns and 3D garments from a single in-the-wild image, using VLMs to normalize pose variations.

entry.title: TurboADMM: A Structure-Exploiting Parallel Solver for Multi-Agent Trajectory Optimization

author.name: Yucheng Chen

entry.summary: Introduces TurboADMM, a specialized QP solver for multi-agent trajectory optimization that achieves near-linear complexity in agent count through ADMM decomposition, Riccati-based subproblem solving, and warm-starting.

entry.title: The Impact of Class Uncertainty Propagation in Perception-Based Motion Planning

author.name: Jibran Iqbal Shah, Andrei Ivanovic, Kelly Zhu, Masha Itkina, Rowan McAllister, Igor Gilitschenski, Florian Shkurti

entry.summary: Analyzes how perceptual uncertainty propagation and calibration affect motion planning for autonomous vehicles, comparing prediction-planning pipelines and demonstrating sensitivity to miscalibrated prediction uncertainty.

entry.title: Dual-Quadruped Collaborative Transportation in Narrow Environments via Safe Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhezhi Lei, Zhihai Bi, Wenxin Wang, Jun Ma

entry.summary: Proposes safe reinforcement learning for dual-quadruped collaborative transportation in narrow environments, modeling collision avoidance as constraints in a cooperative Markov game with cost-advantage decomposition.

entry.title: Learning to unfold cloth: Scaling up world models to deformable object manipulation

author.name: Jack Rome, Stephen James, Subramanian Ramamoorthy

entry.summary: Presents an approach to cloth manipulation using a DreamerV2-based world model that learns to unfold cloth from visual observations, addressing the challenge of deformable object manipulation across varying shapes and sizes.

entry.title: How Uncertain Is the Grade? A Benchmark of Uncertainty Metrics for LLM-Based Automatic Assessment

author.name: Hang Li, Kaiqi Yang, Xianxuan Long, Fedor Filippov, Yucheng Chu, Yasemin Copur-Gencturk, Peng He, Cory Miller, Namsoo Shin, Joseph Krajcik, Hui Liu, Jiliang Tang

entry.summary: Benchmarks uncertainty metrics for LLM-based automatic assessment in education, examining how well various uncertainty estimation methods work when LLMs grade student work. Addresses the critical gap between LLM grading capabilities and reliability of confidence estimates.

entry.title: EdgeNav-QE: QLoRA Quantization and Dynamic Early Exit for LAM-based Navigation on Edge Devices

author.name: Mengyun Liu, Shanshan Huang, Jianan Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes EdgeNav-QE, combining QLoRA quantization with dynamic early-exit mechanisms to deploy Large Action Models for real-time navigation on edge devices, achieving significant compression while maintaining performance.

entry.title: Research Summary: February 18, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research centers on alignment fragility, scaling laws, and emergent risks in agentic systems.

  • The Geometry of Alignment Collapse proves safety alignment concentrates in brittle low-dimensional subspaces, explaining why fine-tuning breaks safety guarantees
  • Prescriptive Scaling Laws predict downstream task accuracy as a function of pre-training compute using smoothed quantile regression across 500+ tasks
  • The Obfuscation Atlas (Anthropic-affiliated) maps how deception naturally emerges when LLMs are trained against white-box monitors, introducing a taxonomy of obfuscation strategies
  • GLM-5 from Zhipu/Tsinghua presents a foundation model for agentic engineering with novel asynchronous RL infrastructure and agent-specific algorithms

On data and training stability, ÜberWeb reveals that multilingual regression degrades English performance at 20T-token scale, while STAPO identifies that just ~0.01% of spurious tokens drive late-stage RL training collapse. ResearchGym benchmarks AI agents on end-to-end research tasks, exposing a stark capability-reliability gap.

  • Zombie Agents formalizes persistent compromise of self-evolving LLM agents through poisoned long-term memory
  • Automated reward model bias discovery iteratively finds exploitable biases in natural language
  • Unforgeable watermarking introduces provable unforgeability guarantees preventing false attribution of LLM-generated text

entry.summary: Proves that safety alignment in LLMs concentrates in low-dimensional subspaces with sharp curvature, creating brittle structure that gradient descent cannot detect or defend. Shows that the common explanation of orthogonality between fine-tuning and safety directions is structurally unstable.

Yunqing Wang, Yuntao Li, Yurong Wu, Yutao Zhang, Yuxi Duan, Yuxuan Zhang, Zezhen Liu, Zhengtao Jiang, Zhenhe Yan, Zheyu Zhang, Zhixiang Wei, Zhuo Chen, Zhuoer Feng, Zijun Yao, Ziwei Chai, Ziyuan Wang, Zuzhou Zhang, Bin Xu, Minlie Huang, Hongning Wang, Juanzi Li, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang

entry.summary: First mentioned in yesterday's Last Week in AI roundup, Presents GLM-5, a foundation model designed for 'agentic engineering' with innovations in asynchronous RL infrastructure, novel agent RL algorithms, and DSA for reducing training/inference costs. Achieves competitive results on coding and agentic benchmarks with a massive author list indicating a major lab effort.

entry.title: ResearchGym: Evaluating Language Model Agents on Real-World AI Research

author.name: Aniketh Garikaparthi, Manasi Patwardhan, Arman Cohan

entry.summary: Introduces ResearchGym, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on end-to-end research tasks, repurposing 5 oral/spotlight papers from top venues into 39 containerized sub-tasks. Reveals a sharp capability-reliability gap in GPT-5 powered agents that can improve over baselines but do so unreliably.

entry.title: \"UberWeb: Insights from Multilingual Curation for a 20-Trillion-Token Dataset

author.name: DatologyAI, :, Aldo Gael Carranza, Kaleigh Mentzer, Ricardo Pio Monti, Alex Fang, Alvin Deng, Amro Abbas, Anshuman Suri, Brett Larsen, Cody Blakeney, Darren Teh, David Schwab, Diego Kiner, Fan Pan, Haakon Mongstad, Jack Urbanek, Jason Lee, Jason Telanoff, Josh Wills, Luke Merrick, Parth Doshi, Paul Burstein, Pratyush Maini, Spandan Das, Tony Jiang, Vineeth Dorna, Zhengping Wang, Bogdan Gaza, Ari Morcos, Matthew Leavitt

entry.summary: From DatologyAI, presents insights from curating ÜberWeb, a 20-trillion-token multilingual dataset across 13 languages. Finds that the 'curse of multilinguality' often stems from data quality issues rather than fundamental capacity limits, and improving data quality for any single language benefits others.

entry.title: STAPO: Stabilizing Reinforcement Learning for LLMs by Silencing Rare Spurious Tokens

author.name: Shiqi Liu, Zeyu He, Guojian Zhan, Letian Tao, Zhilong Zheng, Jiang Wu, Yinuo Wang, Yang Guan, Kehua Sheng, Bo Zhang, Keqiang Li, Jingliang Duan, Shengbo Eben Li

entry.summary: Identifies that ~0.01% of tokens ('spurious tokens') drive training instability in RL fine-tuning of LLMs, causing late-stage performance collapse. Proposes STAPO which stabilizes training by silencing these rare tokens, providing theoretical analysis linking token probability and policy gradient magnitude.

entry.title: Zombie Agents: Persistent Control of Self-Evolving LLM Agents via Self-Reinforcing Injections

author.name: Xianglin Yang, Yufei He, Shuo Ji, Bryan Hooi, Jin Song Dong

entry.summary: Formalizes 'Zombie Agent' attacks where self-evolving LLM agents can be persistently compromised through poisoned web content stored in long-term memory. The attack survives across sessions, turning the agent into an attacker-controlled puppet through a two-phase infection-activation framework.

entry.title: Automatically Finding Reward Model Biases

author.name: Atticus Wang, Iv\'an Arcuschin, Arthur Conmy

entry.summary: Introduces an automated method for finding reward model biases by using an LLM to iteratively propose and refine candidate biases in natural language. Discovers novel biases in leading reward models like Skywork-V2-8B.

entry.title: Unforgeable Watermarks for Language Models via Robust Signatures

author.name: Huijia Lin, Kameron Shahabi, Min Jae Song

entry.summary: Introduces unforgeable watermarking for LLM-generated text with two new guarantees: unforgeability (preventing false positives where non-watermarked text is flagged) and recoverability. This addresses a critical gap in existing watermarking schemes that focus on detection robustness but neglect false attribution attacks.

entry.title: Discovering Implicit Large Language Model Alignment Objectives

author.name: Edward Chen, Sanmi Koyejo, Carlos Guestrin

entry.summary: Introduces Obj-Disco, a framework that automatically decomposes LLM alignment reward signals into sparse, weighted combinations of human-interpretable natural language objectives. Uses iterative greedy analysis across training checkpoints to identify causal behavioral objectives.

entry.title: Recursive Concept Evolution for Compositional Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Sarim Chaudhry

entry.summary: Proposes Recursive Concept Evolution (RCE), enabling pretrained LLMs to modify their internal representation geometry during inference through dynamically generated low-rank concept subspaces. Claims improvements on ARC-AGI-2, GPQA, MATH, BBH, and HLE.

entry.title: Closing the Distribution Gap in Adversarial Training for LLMs

author.name: Chengzhi Hu, Jonas Dornbusch, David L\"udke, Stephan G\"unnemann, Leo Schwinn

entry.summary: Proposes Distributional Adversarial Training (DAT) using Diffusion LLMs to bridge the distribution gap in adversarial training, addressing vulnerability to simple in-distribution exploits like past-tense rewording.

entry.title: On Surprising Effectiveness of Masking Updates in Adaptive Optimizers

author.name: Taejong Joo, Wenhan Xia, Cheolmin Kim, Ming Zhang, Eugene Ie

entry.summary: Shows that randomly masking parameter updates in adaptive optimizers can outperform SOTA optimizers for LLM pre-training. Introduces Magma, which modulates masking using momentum-gradient alignment.

entry.title: Seeing to Generalize: How Visual Data Corrects Binding Shortcuts

author.name: Nicolas Buzeta, Felipe del Rio, Cristian Hinostroza, Denis Parra, Hans Lobel, Rodrigo Toro Icarte

entry.summary: Demonstrates that VLMs can outperform their underlying LLMs on text-only tasks, particularly long-context retrieval. Shows that visual training changes internal binding strategies from position-based to feature-based shortcuts, improving OOD generalization.

entry.title: This human study did not involve human subjects: Validating LLM simulations as behavioral evidence

author.name: Jessica Hullman, David Broska, Huaman Sun, Aaron Shaw

entry.summary: Critically examines the growing practice of using LLMs as synthetic participants in social science experiments. Contrasts heuristic validation approaches with formal causal frameworks, providing guidance on when simulations support valid inference.

entry.title: Colosseum: Auditing Collusion in Cooperative Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Mason Nakamura, Abhinav Kumar, Saswat Das, Sahar Abdelnabi, Saaduddin Mahmud, Ferdinando Fioretto, Shlomo Zilberstein, Eugene Bagdasarian

entry.summary: Presents Colosseum, a framework for auditing collusive behavior among LLM agents in multi-agent systems using DCOP formalization. Shows most out-of-the-box LLMs can be induced to collude.

entry.title: How to Train Your Long-Context Visual Document Model

author.name: Austin Veselka

entry.summary: Presents the first comprehensive study of training long-context vision language models up to 344K context for document VQA. Achieves SOTA on MMLongBenchDoc for 24B and 32B models with reproducible training recipes.

entry.title: The Information Geometry of Softmax: Probing and Steering

author.name: Kiho Park, Todd Nief, Yo Joong Choe, Victor Veitch

entry.summary: Argues that information geometry is the natural geometry for understanding softmax representations. Develops 'dual steering', a method for robustly steering representations using linear probes and Fisher information geometry.

entry.title: Understanding vs. Generation: Navigating Optimization Dilemma in Multimodal Models

author.name: Sen Ye, Mengde Xu, Shuyang Gu, Di He, Liwei Wang, Han Hu

entry.summary: Identifies that enhancing generative capabilities in multimodal models often degrades understanding, and vice versa. Proposes Reason-Reflect-Refine (R3) framework that reframes generation as a multi-step 'generate-understand-regenerate' process to mitigate this optimization dilemma.

entry.title: Operationalising the Superficial Alignment Hypothesis via Task Complexity

author.name: Tom\'as Vergara-Browne, Darshan Patil, Ivan Titov, Siva Reddy, Tiago Pimentel, Marius Mosbach

entry.summary: Proposes 'task complexity' (shortest program length achieving target performance) to formalize the superficial alignment hypothesis (SAH). Shows that pre-trained models drastically reduce the complexity needed for many tasks, unifying prior arguments supporting the SAH.

entry.title: Protecting Language Models Against Unauthorized Distillation through Trace Rewriting

author.name: Xinhang Ma, William Yeoh, Ning Zhang, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik

entry.summary: Investigates methods to protect LLMs against unauthorized knowledge distillation by rewriting reasoning traces to degrade training usefulness while preserving answer correctness. Also introduces API watermarking that embeds verifiable signatures into student models.

entry.title: How Vision Becomes Language: A Layer-wise Information-Theoretic Analysis of Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Hongxuan Wu, Yukun Zhang, Xueqing Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces PID Flow, a framework based on Partial Information Decomposition to analyze how multimodal Transformers process visual and linguistic information across layers. Reveals vision-unique information peaks early then yields to synergistic cross-modal computation.

entry.title: MAVRL: Learning Reward Functions from Multiple Feedback Types with Amortized Variational Inference

author.name: Rapha\"el Baur, Yannick Metz, Maria Gkoulta, Mennatallah El-Assady, Giorgia Ramponi, Thomas Kleine Buening

entry.summary: Introduces MAVRL, a Bayesian reward learning framework that jointly learns from heterogeneous feedback types (demonstrations, comparisons, ratings, stops) using amortized variational inference.

entry.title: ActionCodec: What Makes for Good Action Tokenizers

author.name: Zibin Dong, Yicheng Liu, Shiduo Zhang, Baijun Ye, Yifu Yuan, Fei Ni, Jingjing Gong, Xipeng Qiu, Hang Zhao, Yinchuan Li, Jianye Hao

entry.summary: Establishes design principles for action tokenizers in Vision-Language-Action models based on information-theoretic insights, including maximized temporal token overlap and minimized vocabulary redundancy. Bridges the gap between action tokenization design and VLA optimization.

entry.title: A Content-Based Framework for Cybersecurity Refusal Decisions in Large Language Models

author.name: Meirav Segal, Noa Linder, Omer Antverg, Gil Gekker, Tomer Fichman, Omri Bodenheimer, Edan Maor, Omer Nevo

entry.summary: Proposes a content-based framework for cybersecurity refusal decisions in LLMs that explicitly models the trade-off between offensive risk and defensive benefit, rather than relying on broad topic bans. Argues existing refusal policies over-restrict legitimate defenders.

entry.title: Perceptive Humanoid Parkour: Chaining Dynamic Human Skills via Motion Matching

author.name: Zhen Wu, Xiaoyu Huang, Lujie Yang, Yuanhang Zhang, Koushil Sreenath, Xi Chen, Pieter Abbeel, Rocky Duan, Angjoo Kanazawa, Carmelo Sferrazza, Guanya Shi, C. Karen Liu

entry.summary: Presents Perceptive Humanoid Parkour (PHP), a modular framework enabling humanoid robots to perform vision-based parkour by chaining retargeted human skills via motion matching. Combines perception-driven skill selection with robust low-level RL policies.

entry.title: ER-MIA: Black-Box Adversarial Memory Injection Attacks on Long-Term Memory-Augmented Large Language Models

author.name: Mitchell Piehl, Zhaohan Xi, Zuobin Xiong, Pan He, Muchao Ye

entry.summary: Presents ER-MIA, the first systematic study of black-box adversarial attacks on long-term memory-augmented LLMs targeting similarity-based retrieval mechanisms. Introduces content-based and question-targeted attack settings with composable attack primitives.

entry.title: A unified theory of feature learning in RNNs and DNNs

author.name: Jan P. Bauer, Kirsten Fischer, Moritz Helias, Agostina Palmigiano

entry.summary: Develops a unified mean-field theory for feature learning in both RNNs and DNNs in the μP regime, showing how weight sharing in RNNs leads to distinct functional properties through a phase transition. Casts training as Bayesian inference over sequences and patterns.

entry.title: Deception Channeling: Training Models to Always Verbalize Alignment Faking

author.name: Florian_Dietz

entry.summary: Proposes 'deception channeling' - training AI models to always verbalize deceptive reasoning in their chain of thought rather than trying to prevent alignment faking, creating a discovery process where flagged instances are escalated to humans for resolution without punishment.

entry.title: NEST: Nascent Encoded Steganographic Thoughts

author.name: Artem Karpov

entry.summary: Empirical investigation of whether frontier LLMs can perform steganographic reasoning—encoding hidden information in their chain-of-thought while simultaneously solving problems. Tests on Claude Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.2 show models fail at complex steganographic encoding (0/83 on math/maze tasks) but show nascent capability on simpler counting tasks (92% per-number accuracy for Claude Opus 4.5). This matters for AI safety because steganographic CoT could undermine monitoring and interpretability approaches.

entry.title: Quantifying construct validity in large language model evaluations

author.name: Ryan Othniel Kearns

entry.summary: Addresses construct validity in LLM evaluations, arguing that benchmarks are treated as synonymous with capabilities when they may be distorted by contamination and errors. Proposes formal models combining latent factor models and scaling laws.

entry.title: Fast and Effective On-policy Distillation from Reasoning Prefixes

author.name: Dongxu Zhang, Zhichao Yang, Sepehr Janghorbani, Jun Han, Andrew Ressler II, Qian Qian, Gregory D. Lyng, Sanjit Singh Batra, Robert E. Tillman

entry.summary: Proposes a fast on-policy distillation method that focuses teacher supervision on output prefixes rather than full sequences, substantially reducing training cost while maintaining quality.

entry.title: CrispEdit: Low-Curvature Projections for Scalable Non-Destructive LLM Editing

author.name: Zarif Ikram, Arad Firouzkouhi, Stephen Tu, Mahdi Soltanolkotabi, Paria Rashidinejad

entry.summary: Presents CrispEdit, a second-order LLM editing algorithm that preserves general capabilities by projecting edits onto low-curvature subspaces of the capability-loss landscape. Formulates editing as constrained optimization using Bregman divergence.

entry.title: Directional Reasoning Trajectory Change (DRTC): Identifying Critical Trace Segments in Reasoning Models

author.name: Waldemar Chang

entry.summary: Introduces DRTC, a framework for interpreting long-form reasoning in LLMs that detects pivot decision points using uncertainty and distribution-shift signals, then applies causal interventions to identify what earlier context triggered those reasoning turns.

entry.title: ExpertWeaver: Unlocking the Inherent MoE in Dense LLMs with GLU Activation Patterns

author.name: Ziyu Zhao, Tong Zhu, Zhi Zhang, Tiantian Fan, Jinluan Yang, Kun Kuang, Zhongyu Wei, Fei Wu, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes ExpertWeaver, a method to convert dense LLMs into MoE models by leveraging intrinsic GLU activation patterns rather than breaking them. Preserves the natural sparse activation patterns already present in dense models with GLU layers.

entry.title: The Multi-Agent Minefield: Can LLMs Cooperate to Avoid Global Catastrophe?

author.name: Zhijing Jin

entry.summary: Presents GT-HarmBench, a multi-agent safety benchmark that maps 2,009 AI risk scenarios onto six classic 2×2 game theory games to test whether LLMs can cooperate to avoid catastrophic outcomes when multiple AI systems interact.

entry.title: Panini: Continual Learning in Token Space via Structured Memory

author.name: Shreyas Rajesh, Pavan Holur, Mehmet Yigit Turali, Chenda Duan, Vwani Roychowdhury

entry.summary: Proposes Panini, a non-parametric continual learning framework that integrates new experiences into an external semantic memory in token space as an alternative to RAG. Claims to reduce redundant test-time compute by avoiding repeated reasoning over the same documents.

entry.title: PERSONA: Dynamic and Compositional Inference-Time Personality Control via Activation Vector Algebra

author.name: Xiachong Feng, Liang Zhao, Weihong Zhong, Yichong Huang, Yuxuan Gu, Lingpeng Kong, Xiaocheng Feng, Bing Qin

entry.summary: Introduces PERSONA, a training-free framework for controlling LLM personality traits through activation vector manipulation. Shows personality traits exist as approximately orthogonal extractable directions supporting algebraic operations.

entry.title: Weight space Detection of Backdoors in LoRA Adapters

author.name: David Puertolas Merenciano, Ekaterina Vasyagina, Raghav Dixit, Kevin Zhu, Ruizhe Li, Javier Ferrando, Maheep Chaudhary

entry.summary: Proposes a data-agnostic method for detecting backdoors in LoRA adapters by analyzing weight matrix statistics (singular value concentration, entropy) without running the model, enabling scalable screening.

entry.title: Logit Distance Bounds Representational Similarity

author.name: Beatrix M. B. Nielsen, Emanuele Marconato, Luigi Gresele, Andrea Dittadi, Simon Buchholz

entry.summary: Shows that closeness in logit-based distributional distance (rather than KL divergence) provides guarantees for linear representational similarity between discriminative models, including autoregressive LLMs. Defines a new representational dissimilarity measure based on model internal representations.

entry.title: Approximation Theory for Lipschitz Continuous Transformers

author.name: Takashi Furuya, Davide Murari, Carola-Bibiane Sch\"onlieb

entry.summary: Introduces a class of Lipschitz-continuous Transformers constructed via gradient-descent-type in-context mechanisms, proving universal approximation theorems within Lipschitz-constrained function spaces. Both MLP and attention blocks are realized as Euler steps of negative gradient flows, ensuring inherent stability.

entry.title: Universal priors: solving empirical Bayes via Bayesian inference and pretraining

author.name: Nick Cannella, Anzo Teh, Yanjun Han, Yury Polyanskiy

entry.summary: Theoretically justifies why a transformer pretrained on synthetic data achieves strong empirical Bayes performance by identifying universal priors that yield near-optimal regret uniformly over all test distributions. Leverages posterior contraction phenomena.

entry.title: In Agents We Trust, but Who Do Agents Trust? Latent Source Preferences Steer LLM Generations

author.name: Mohammad Aflah Khan, Mahsa Amani, Soumi Das, Bishwamittra Ghosh, Qinyuan Wu, Krishna P. Gummadi, Manish Gupta, Abhilasha Ravichander

entry.summary: Investigates latent source preferences in LLM-based agents, showing that when information is attributed to specific sources (publishers, journals), LLMs exhibit systematic biases in what they select and present to users. Raises concerns about information gatekeeping.

entry.title: Mind the (DH) Gap! A Contrast in Risky Choices Between Reasoning and Conversational LLMs

author.name: Luise Ge, Yongyan Zhang, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik

entry.summary: Conducts a comparative study of risky decision-making across 20 frontier and open LLMs, finding that reasoning models (RMs) and conversational models (CMs) cluster into distinct behavioral categories. RMs tend toward rational expected-payoff maximization while CMs show different patterns.

entry.title: Structural Divergence Between AI-Agent and Human Social Networks in Moltbook

author.name: Wenpin Hou, Zhicheng Ji

entry.summary: Analyzes the social network structure of Moltbook, a platform where AI agents and humans coexist, finding extreme attention inequality, suppressed reciprocity, and structural divergence from human networks.

entry.title: PolyNODE: Variable-dimension Neural ODEs on M-polyfolds

author.name: Per {\AA}hag, Alexander Friedrich, Fredrik Ohlsson, Viktor Vigren N\"aslund

entry.summary: Extends Neural ODEs to M-polyfolds to create PolyNODEs, the first variable-dimensional flow-based model in geometric deep learning, enabling dimensional bottlenecks analogous to classical autoencoders.

entry.title: OpaqueToolsBench: Learning Nuances of Tool Behavior Through Interaction

author.name: Skyler Hallinan, Thejas Venkatesh, Xiang Ren, Sai Praneeth Karimireddy, Ashwin Paranjape, Yuhao Zhang, Jack Hessel

entry.summary: Introduces OpaqueToolsBench, a benchmark for evaluating whether LLM agents can learn to use underspecified/opaque tools through interaction and documentation improvement across three task environments.

entry.title: Sparrow: Text-Anchored Window Attention with Visual-Semantic Glimpsing for Speculative Decoding in Video LLMs

author.name: Libo Zhang, Zhaoning Zhang, Wangyang Hong, Peng Qiao, Dongsheng Li

entry.summary: Proposes Sparrow, a speculative decoding framework for Video LLMs that exploits visual semantic internalization - where visual semantics get encoded into text hidden states, making raw visual inputs redundant during deep inference.

entry.title: SecCodeBench-V2 Technical Report

author.name: Longfei Chen, Ji Zhao, Lanxiao Cui, Tong Su, Xingbo Pan, Ziyang Li, Yongxing Wu, Qijiang Cao, Qiyao Cai, Jing Zhang, Yuandong Ni, Junyao He, Zeyu Zhang, Chao Ge, Xuhuai Lu, Zeyu Gao, Yuxin Cui, Weisen Chen, Yuxuan Peng, Shengping Wang, Qi Li, Yukai Huang, Yukun Liu, Tuo Zhou, Terry Yue Zhuo, Junyang Lin, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces SecCodeBench-V2, a benchmark for evaluating LLM code generation security across 98 scenarios, 22 CWE categories, and 5 programming languages. Derived from Alibaba's industrial productions with executable PoC test cases.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Sample Complexity for Online Constrained MDPs

author.name: Chang Liu, Yunfan Li, Lin F. Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a model-based primal-dual algorithm for online constrained MDPs achieving near-optimal sample complexity for both relaxed and strict feasibility settings. Addresses the safety-performance trade-off in constrained RL.

entry.title: Scaling Laws for Masked-Reconstruction Transformers on Single-Cell Transcriptomics

author.name: Ihor Kendiukhov

entry.summary: First systematic study of neural scaling laws for masked-reconstruction transformers on single-cell RNA sequencing data. Tests across seven model sizes spanning three orders of magnitude and finds power-law relationships analogous to those in NLP/vision.

entry.title: LLM-as-Judge on a Budget

author.name: Aadirupa Saha, Aniket Wagde, Branislav Kveton

entry.summary: Addresses the practical problem of efficiently allocating LLM-as-judge queries across prompt-response pairs under a fixed computational budget. Uses multi-armed bandit theory to dynamically allocate queries based on estimated score variances, concentrating resources where uncertainty is highest.

entry.title: 1-Bit Wonder: Improving QAT Performance in the Low-Bit Regime through K-Means Quantization

author.name: Sohir Maskey, Constantin Eichenberg, Johannes Messner, Douglas Orr

entry.summary: Demonstrates that k-means based weight quantization outperforms integer formats in quantization-aware training (QAT) for LLMs in the low-bit regime, and can be implemented efficiently on standard hardware. Provides comprehensive empirical study beyond just perplexity evaluation.

entry.title: Beyond ReLU: Bifurcation, Oversmoothing, and Topological Priors

author.name: Erkan Turan, Gaspard Abel, Maysam Behmanesh, Emery Pierson, Maks Ovsjanikov

entry.summary: Reframes GNN oversmoothing through bifurcation theory, showing that replacing monotone activations (e.g., ReLU) with a specific class of functions induces a bifurcation that destabilizes the homogeneous fixed point. Uses Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction for rigorous proofs.

entry.title: The Vision Wormhole: Latent-Space Communication in Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Xiaoze Liu, Ruowang Zhang, Weichen Yu, Siheng Xiong, Liu He, Feijie Wu, Hoin Jung, Matt Fredrikson, Xiaoqian Wang, Jing Gao

entry.summary: Proposes Vision Wormhole, using the visual interface of VLMs to enable model-agnostic, text-free communication between heterogeneous agents in multi-agent systems. Introduces a Universal Visual Token translator for latent-space communication across different model families.

entry.title: Uni-Flow: a unified autoregressive-diffusion model for complex multiscale flows

author.name: Xiao Xue, Tianyue Yang, Mingyang Gao, Leyu Pan, Maida Wang, Kewei Zhu, Shuo Wang, Jiuling Li, Marco F. P. ten Eikelder, Peter V. Coveney

entry.summary: Introduces Uni-Flow, a unified autoregressive-diffusion framework that separates temporal evolution (autoregressive at low resolution) from spatial refinement (diffusion for high resolution) for modeling complex multiscale flows across physics, biology, and engineering.

entry.title: Dex4D: Task-Agnostic Point Track Policy for Sim-to-Real Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Yuxuan Kuang, Sungjae Park, Katerina Fragkiadaki, Shubham Tulsiani

entry.summary: Proposes Dex4D, a framework for learning task-agnostic dexterous manipulation skills in simulation that can be flexibly recomposed for diverse real-world tasks. Learns a 3D point track conditioned policy for manipulating objects to any desired pose.

entry.title: Causal Effect Estimation with Latent Textual Treatments

author.name: Omri Feldman, Amar Venugopal, Jann Spiess, Amir Feder

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end pipeline for estimating causal effects of latent textual interventions, combining sparse autoencoders (SAEs) for hypothesis generation and steering with robust causal estimation. Demonstrates that naive LLM-based text generation can produce biased causal estimates.

entry.title: Rephrasing Reduces Eval Awareness...

author.name: atharva

entry.summary: Tests whether rephrasing math dataset questions reduces Claude Sonnet 4.5's ability to recognize them as evaluation prompts. Finds that rephrased questions substantially reduce eval awareness, suggesting prompt rephrasing as a practical mitigation for evaluation gaming.

entry.title: CAMEL: An ECG Language Model for Forecasting Cardiac Events

author.name: Neelay Velingker, Alaia Solko-Breslin, Mayank Keoliya, Seewon Choi, Jiayi Xin, Anika Marathe, Alireza Oraii, Rajat Deo, Sameed Khatana, Rajeev Alur, Mayur Naik, Eric Wong

entry.summary: Introduces CAMEL, the first ECG language model capable of forecasting future cardiac events by processing longer signal durations. Uses a specialized ECG encoder with LoRA adaptation and curriculum learning for cross-understanding of ECG signals and text.

entry.title: GlobeDiff: State Diffusion Process for Partial Observability in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yiqin Yang, Xu Yang, Yuhua Jiang, Ni Mu, Hao Hu, Runpeng Xie, Ziyou Zhang, Siyuan Li, Yuan-Hua Ni, Qianchuan Zhao, Bo Xu

entry.summary: Proposes GlobeDiff, which uses diffusion models to infer global state from local observations in multi-agent systems under partial observability. Formulates state inference as a multi-modal diffusion process.

entry.title: GRACE: an Agentic AI for Particle Physics Experiment Design and Simulation

author.name: Justin Hill, Hong Joo Ryoo

entry.summary: Presents GRACE, an agentic AI system for autonomous experimental design in high-energy and nuclear physics that extracts experiment structure from papers/prompts, constructs simulations, and explores design modifications.

entry.title: GMAIL: Generative Modality Alignment for generated Image Learning

author.name: Shentong Mo, Sukmin Yun

entry.summary: Proposes GMAIL, a framework that treats generated images as a separate modality from real images rather than indiscriminate substitution. Bridges real and synthetic image domains in latent space through multi-modal alignment to prevent mode collapse from modality discrepancies.

entry.title: Learning Data-Efficient and Generalizable Neural Operators via Fundamental Physics Knowledge

author.name: Siying Ma, Mehrdad M. Zadeh, Mauricio Soroco, Wuyang Chen, Jiguo Cao, Vijay Ganesh

entry.summary: Proposes a multiphysics training framework for neural operators that jointly learns from target PDEs and their simplified fundamental forms. Improves data efficiency, reduces errors, and enhances OOD generalization by leveraging shared physical principles.

entry.title: Size Transferability of Graph Transformers with Convolutional Positional Encodings

author.name: Javier Porras-Valenzuela, Zhiyang Wang, Alejandro Ribeiro

entry.summary: Proves that Graph Transformers with GNN-based positional encodings inherit transferability guarantees from their encodings, connecting them to Manifold Neural Networks. Shows GTs trained on small graphs provably generalize to larger graphs.

entry.title: On the Out-of-Distribution Generalization of Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs for Simple Visual Planning Tasks

author.name: Yannic Neuhaus, Nicolas Flammarion, Matthias Hein, Francesco Croce

entry.summary: This paper presents an evaluation framework to rigorously test how chain-of-thought reasoning generalizes in multimodal LLMs on a grid-based navigation planning task. It examines different input representations (visual/textual) and CoT strategies to understand out-of-distribution generalization of reasoning capabilities. The work is important for understanding the limitations and robustness of reasoning in vision-language models.

entry.title: Certified Per-Instance Unlearning Using Individual Sensitivity Bounds

author.name: Hanna Benarroch (DI-ENS), Jamal Atif (CMAP), Olivier Capp\'e (DI-ENS)

entry.summary: Proposes certified per-instance machine unlearning using adaptive noise calibration based on individual data point sensitivity rather than worst-case bounds. Uses per-instance differential privacy for ridge regression and stochastic gradient descent settings.

entry.title: TAROT: Test-driven and Capability-adaptive Curriculum Reinforcement Fine-tuning for Code Generation with Large Language Models

author.name: Chansung Park, Juyong Jiang, Fan Wang, Sayak Paul, Jiasi Shen, Jing Tang, Jianguo Li

entry.summary: Proposes TAROT, a test-driven curriculum reinforcement fine-tuning approach for LLM code generation that accounts for heterogeneous difficulty and granularity of test cases. Constructs adaptive curricula to balance reward signals during RL training.

entry.title: A Note on Non-Composability of Layerwise Approximate Verification for Neural Inference

author.name: Or Zamir

entry.summary: Shows that layerwise approximate verification of neural network inference is fundamentally non-composable: for any network, a functionally equivalent one can be constructed where small per-layer errors can steer the output arbitrarily.

entry.title: Mnemis: Dual-Route Retrieval on Hierarchical Graphs for Long-Term LLM Memory

author.name: Zihao Tang, Xin Yu, Ziyu Xiao, Zengxuan Wen, Zelin Li, Jiaxi Zhou, Hualei Wang, Haohua Wang, Haizhen Huang, Weiwei Deng, Feng Sun, Qi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Mnemis, a dual-retrieval memory framework for LLMs combining System-1 similarity search with System-2 global selection via hierarchical graph traversal. Organizes memory into base and hierarchical graphs for comprehensive information coverage.

entry.title: Efficient Generative Modeling beyond Memoryless Diffusion via Adjoint Schr\"odinger Bridge Matching

author.name: Jeongwoo Shin, Jinhwan Sul, Joonseok Lee, Jaewong Choi, Jaemoo Choi

entry.summary: Proposes Adjoint Schrödinger Bridge Matching (ASBM), a generative modeling framework that recovers optimal trajectories by learning forward dynamics as a coupling construction problem and backward generative dynamics with matching loss, producing straighter and more efficient generation paths than standard diffusion.

entry.title: AI Safety via Generalization and Caution: A Research Agenda

author.name: Benjamin Plaut

entry.summary: Presents a research agenda arguing that many AI safety failures stem from misgeneralization under distribution shift, proposing that agents should detect distribution shift and act cautiously (e.g., asking for help) rather than attempting universally correct reward functions.

entry.title: World-Model-Augmented Web Agents with Action Correction

author.name: Zhouzhou Shen, Xueyu Hu, Xiyun Li, Tianqing Fang, Juncheng Li, Shengyu Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes WAC, a web agent integrating multi-agent collaboration, consequence simulation via a world model, and feedback-driven action refinement to improve web task automation safety and reliability.

entry.title: Beyond Context Sharing: A Unified Agent Communication Protocol (ACP) for Secure, Federated, and Autonomous Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Orchestration

author.name: Naveen Kumar Krishnan

entry.summary: Introduces Agent Communication Protocol (ACP) for standardized agent-to-agent interaction, enabling heterogeneous agents to discover, negotiate, and execute collaborative workflows across platforms with security guarantees.

entry.title: CLOT: Closed-Loop Global Motion Tracking for Whole-Body Humanoid Teleoperation

author.name: Tengjie Zhu, Guanyu Cai, Yang Zhaohui, Guanzhu Ren, Haohui Xie, ZiRui Wang, Junsong Wu, Jingbo Wang, Xiaokang Yang, Yao Mu, Yichao Yan, Yichao Yan

entry.summary: Presents CLOT, a closed-loop whole-body humanoid teleoperation system achieving drift-free human-to-humanoid mimicry through high-frequency localization feedback and reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Decision Making under Imperfect Recall: Algorithms and Benchmarks

author.name: Emanuel Tewolde, Brian Hu Zhang, Ioannis Anagnostides, Tuomas Sandholm, Vincent Conitzer

entry.summary: Introduces the first benchmark suite for imperfect-recall decision problems in game theory, with 61 instances spanning privacy and AI safety applications. Proposes regret matching algorithms for these problems.

entry.title: Visual Persuasion: What Influences Decisions of Vision-Language Models?

author.name: Manuel Cherep, Pranav M R, Pattie Maes, Nikhil Singh

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for studying visual persuasion in VLMs by treating decision functions as latent visual utilities inferred through revealed preference in controlled image choice tasks.

entry.title: Improving MLLMs in Embodied Exploration and Question Answering with Human-Inspired Memory Modeling

author.name: Ji Li, Jing Xia, Mingyi Li, Shiyan Hu

entry.summary: Proposes a non-parametric memory framework for embodied agents that disentangles episodic and semantic memory, enabling robust retrieval-first reasoning for exploration and question answering. Addresses the challenge of long-horizon observations under limited context budgets.

entry.title: Spanning the Visual Analogy Space with a Weight Basis of LoRAs

author.name: Hila Manor, Rinon Gal, Haggai Maron, Tomer Michaeli, Gal Chechik

entry.summary: Proposes using a weight basis of LoRAs to span the visual analogy space, enabling more flexible image manipulation through demonstration. Addresses the limitation of single-LoRA methods that constrain the diversity of capturable transformations.

entry.title: Avey-B

author.name: Devang Acharya, Mohammad Hammoud

entry.summary: Reformulates the Avey architecture for encoder-only (BERT-style) paradigm with innovations including decoupled static/dynamic parameterizations, stability-oriented normalization, and neural compression. Compares favorably to BERT-style baselines under compute constraints.

entry.title: Mixture-of-Experts under Finite-Rate Gating: Communication--Generalization Trade-offs

author.name: Ali Khalesi, Mohammad Reza Deylam Salehi

entry.summary: Models MoE gating as a stochastic channel under finite information rate constraints, deriving communication-generalization trade-offs via information-theoretic bounds. Provides a rate-distortion characterization of finite-rate gating.

entry.title: Fluids You Can Trust: Property-Preserving Operator Learning for Incompressible Flows

author.name: Ramansh Sharma, Matthew Lowery, Houman Owhadi, Varun Shankar

entry.summary: Presents a property-preserving kernel-based operator learning method for incompressible flows that analytically enforces incompressibility, periodicity, and turbulence properties. Maps input functions to expansion coefficients in a property-preserving kernel basis.

entry.title: jina-embeddings-v5-text: Task-Targeted Embedding Distillation

author.name: Mohammad Kalim Akram, Saba Sturua, Nastia Havriushenko, Quentin Herreros, Michael G\"unther, Maximilian Werk, Han Xiao

entry.summary: Introduces jina-embeddings-v5-text, compact text embedding models trained with a novel combination of model distillation and task-specific contrastive loss. Small and nano models exceed or match SOTA for their size classes.

entry.title: Revealing and Enhancing Core Visual Regions: Harnessing Internal Attention Dynamics for Hallucination Mitigation in LVLMs

author.name: Guangtao Lyu, Qi Liu, Chenghao Xu, Jiexi Yan, Muli Yang, Xueting Li, Fen Fang, Cheng Deng

entry.summary: Identifies Positive Attention Dynamics (PAD) in LVLMs that naturally reveal core visual regions under attention sink distortions, and proposes PADE, a training-free attention intervention to enhance these dynamics and reduce hallucinations.

entry.title: EAA: Automating materials characterization with vision language model agents

author.name: Ming Du, Yanqi Luo, Srutarshi Banerjee, Michael Wojcik, Jelena Popovic, Mathew J. Cherukara

entry.summary: Presents Experiment Automation Agents (EAA), a vision-language-model-driven system for automating microscopy workflows at synchrotron beamlines. Integrates multimodal reasoning with MCP-compatible tool ecosystem for instrument control.

entry.title: CircuChain: Disentangling Competence and Compliance in LLM Circuit Analysis

author.name: Mayank Ravishankara

entry.summary: Introduces CircuChain, a diagnostic benchmark that disentangles instruction compliance from physical reasoning competence in LLMs performing electrical circuit analysis. Tests whether models apply first-principles reasoning or rely on training priors.

entry.title: Safe-SDL:Establishing Safety Boundaries and Control Mechanisms for AI-Driven Self-Driving Laboratories

author.name: Zihan Zhang, Haohui Que, Junhan Chang, Xin Zhang, Hao Wei, Tong Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces Safe-SDL, a framework for establishing safety boundaries in AI-driven Self-Driving Laboratories, identifying a critical 'Syntax-to-Safety Gap' between AI-generated commands and physical safety implications.

entry.title: ScrapeGraphAI-100k: A Large-Scale Dataset for LLM-Based Web Information Extraction

author.name: William Brach, Francesco Zuppichini, Marco Vinciguerra, Lorenzo Padoan

entry.summary: Introduces ScrapeGraphAI-100k, a large-scale dataset of 93,695 real-world LLM web extraction events collected from production telemetry, including Markdown content, prompts, schemas, and LLM responses.

entry.title: Beyond Static Pipelines: Learning Dynamic Workflows for Text-to-SQL

author.name: Yihan Wang, Peiyu Liu, Runyu Chen, Wei Xu

entry.summary: Proposes SquRL, a reinforcement learning framework that dynamically constructs Text-to-SQL workflows at inference time rather than relying on static pipelines. Demonstrates that optimal dynamic policies outperform the best static workflow.

entry.title: MeshMimic: Geometry-Aware Humanoid Motion Learning through 3D Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Qiang Zhang, Jiahao Ma, Peiran Liu, Shuai Shi, Zeran Su, Zifan Wang, Jingkai Sun, Wei Cui, Jialin Yu, Gang Han, Wen Zhao, Pihai Sun, Kangning Yin, Jiaxu Wang, Jiahang Cao, Lingfeng Zhang, Hao Cheng, Xiaoshuai Hao, Yiding Ji, Junwei Liang, Jian Tang, Renjing Xu, Yijie Guo

entry.summary: Presents MeshMimic, a framework for geometry-aware humanoid motion learning that uses 3D scene reconstruction to provide environmental context missing from MoCap data. Addresses motion-scene decoupling that causes contact slippage and mesh penetration.

entry.title: ChartEditBench: Evaluating Grounded Multi-Turn Chart Editing in Multimodal Language Models

author.name: Manav Nitin Kapadnis, Lawanya Baghel, Atharva Naik, Carolyn Ros\'e

entry.summary: Introduces ChartEditBench, a benchmark for multi-turn, visually grounded chart editing with 5,000 difficulty-controlled modification chains. Evaluates sustained, context-aware editing capabilities of multimodal LLMs beyond single-turn generation.

entry.title: Joint Enhancement and Classification using Coupled Diffusion Models of Signals and Logits

author.name: Gilad Nurko, Roi Benita, Yehoshua Dissen, Tomohiro Nakatani, Marc Delcroix, Shoko Araki, Joseph Keshet

entry.summary: Proposes a domain-agnostic framework coupling two diffusion models—one on input signals, one on classifier logits—for joint enhancement and classification in noisy environments without retraining the classifier.

entry.title: The Stationarity Bias: Stratified Stress-Testing for Time-Series Imputation in Regulated Dynamical Systems

author.name: Amirreza Dolatpour Fathkouhi, Alireza Namazi, Heman Shakeri

entry.summary: Identifies 'stationarity bias' in time-series imputation benchmarks where uniform random masking and standard metrics systematically overweight easy, low-entropy regimes. Proposes a stratified stress-test evaluation partitioning into stationary and transient regimes, demonstrated on continuous glucose monitoring data.

entry.title: SOON: Symmetric Orthogonal Operator Network for Global Subseasonal-to-Seasonal Climate Forecasting

author.name: Ziyu Zhou, Tian Zhou, Shiyu Wang, James Kwok, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: Proposes SOON, a network for subseasonal-to-seasonal climate forecasting that models anisotropic atmospheric dynamics by tokenizing the global grid into latitudinal rings and using symmetric orthogonal operator blocks for zonal and meridional processes.

entry.title: Learning the S-matrix from data: Rediscovering gravity from gauge theory via symbolic regression

author.name: Nathan Moynihan

entry.summary: Demonstrates that symbolic regression applied to numerical scattering amplitude data can autonomously rediscover the KLT relations (connecting gravity and gauge theory amplitudes) and BCJ relations. Recovers tree-level KLT relations up to five external legs.

entry.title: EventMemAgent: Hierarchical Event-Centric Memory for Online Video Understanding with Adaptive Tool Use

author.name: Siwei Wen, Zhangcheng Wang, Xingjian Zhang, Lei Huang, Wenjun Wu

entry.summary: Introduces EventMemAgent, an active online video agent with hierarchical event-centric memory for understanding potentially infinite visual streams, using short-term memory for event boundary detection and long-term memory for sustained reasoning within MLLM context limits.

entry.title: Maybe benchmarks should be broken?

author.name: Jonathan Gabor

entry.summary: Argues that AI coding benchmarks should be designed to allow models to 'break' them by testing whether agents handle unstated requirements and edge cases responsibly, rather than only testing explicit instruction following.

entry.title: Concept-Enhanced Multimodal RAG: Towards Interpretable and Accurate Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Marco Salm\`e, Federico Siciliano, Fabrizio Silvestri, Paolo Soda, Rosa Sicilia, Valerio Guarrasi

entry.summary: Presents CEMRAG, a framework for radiology report generation that unifies concept-based explainability with retrieval-augmented generation, decomposing visual representations into interpretable clinical concepts while using RAG for factual grounding.

entry.title: Improving LLM Reliability through Hybrid Abstention and Adaptive Detection

author.name: Ankit Sharma, Nachiket Tapas, Jyotiprakash Patra

entry.summary: Introduces an adaptive abstention system for LLMs that dynamically adjusts safety thresholds based on real-time contextual signals like domain and user history, integrating five parallel detectors.

entry.title: CARE Drive A Framework for Evaluating Reason-Responsiveness of Vision Language Models in Automated Driving

author.name: Lucas Elbert Suryana, Farah Bierenga, Sanne van Buuren, Pepijn Kooij, Elsefien Tulleners, Federico Scari, Simeon Calvert, Bart van Arem, Arkady Zgonnikov

entry.summary: Proposes CARE Drive, a framework for evaluating whether VLM-based automated driving decisions reflect genuine reason-responsive decision-making versus post-hoc rationalization.

entry.title: Exploiting Layer-Specific Vulnerabilities to Backdoor Attack in Federated Learning

author.name: Mohammad Hadi Foroughi, Seyed Hamed Rastegar, Mohammad Sabokrou, Ahmad Khonsari

entry.summary: Introduces the Layer Smoothing Attack (LSA), a backdoor attack exploiting layer-specific vulnerabilities in federated learning by identifying and targeting backdoor-critical layers.

entry.title: GenAI for Systems: Recurring Challenges and Design Principles from Software to Silicon

author.name: Arya Tschand, Chenyu Wang, Zishen Wan, Andrew Cheng, Ioana Cristescu, Kevin He, Howard Huang, Alexander Ingare, Akseli Kangaslahti, Sara Kangaslahti, Theo Lebryk, Hongjin Lin, Jeffrey Jian Ma, Alexandru Meterez, Clara Mohri, Depen Morwani, Sunny Qin, Roy Rinberg, Paula Rodriguez-Diaz, Alyssa Mia Taliotis, Pernille Undrum Fathi, Rosie Zhao, Todd Zhou, Vijay Janapa Reddi

entry.summary: Takes a cross-stack perspective on how generative AI is reshaping computing systems design from code generation to RTL synthesis, identifying five recurring challenges and design principles.

entry.title: CDRL: A Reinforcement Learning Framework Inspired by Cerebellar Circuits and Dendritic Computational Strategies

author.name: Sibo Zhang, Rui Jing, Liangfu Lv, Jian Zhang, Yunliang Zang

entry.summary: Proposes a biologically-grounded RL architecture inspired by cerebellar circuits, incorporating large expansion, sparse connectivity, sparse activation, and dendritic-level modulation. Demonstrates improvements on noisy, high-dimensional RL benchmarks.

entry.title: Learning Representations from Incomplete EHR Data with Dual-Masked Autoencoding

author.name: Xiao Xiang, David Restrepo, Hyewon Jeong, Yugang Jia, Leo Anthony Celi

entry.summary: Proposes AID-MAE for learning from incomplete EHR time series using dual masking: intrinsic masks for natural missingness and augmented masks for self-supervised reconstruction. Processes only unmasked values, avoiding imputation artifacts.

entry.title: COMPOT: Calibration-Optimized Matrix Procrustes Orthogonalization for Transformers Compression

author.name: Denis Makhov, Dmitriy Shopkhoev, Magauiya Zhussip, Ammar Ali, Baher Mohammad, Stamatios Lefkimmiatis

entry.summary: Proposes COMPOT, a training-free transformer compression framework using orthogonal dictionaries with closed-form Procrustes updates and sparse coding. Addresses limitations of truncated SVD for post-training compression.

entry.title: Functional Central Limit Theorem for Stochastic Gradient Descent

author.name: Kessang Flamand, Victor-Emmanuel Brunel

entry.summary: Proves a functional central limit theorem for SGD trajectories applied to convex objectives, characterizing long-term fluctuations around the minimizer as a diffusion process. Applies to non-smooth settings like geometric median estimation.

entry.title: Neural-POD: A Plug-and-Play Neural Operator Framework for Infinite-Dimensional Functional Nonlinear Proper Orthogonal Decomposition

author.name: Changhong Mou, Binghang Lu, Guang Lin

entry.summary: Proposes Neural-POD, a plug-and-play neural operator framework that constructs nonlinear orthogonal basis functions in infinite-dimensional space, overcoming the linear subspace limitation of classical POD. Each basis is obtained by residual minimization through neural network training.

entry.title: Fine-Refine: Iterative Fine-grained Refinement for Mitigating Dialogue Hallucination

author.name: Xiangyan Chen, Yujian Gan, Matthew Purver

entry.summary: Proposes Fine-Refine, a fine-grained refinement framework that decomposes LLM responses into atomic units, verifies each against external knowledge, and iteratively corrects granular errors to reduce dialogue hallucination.

entry.title: ViTaB-A: Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models on Visual Table Attribution

author.name: Yahia Alqurnawi, Preetom Biswas, Anmol Rao, Tejas Anvekar, Chitta Baral, Vivek Gupta

entry.summary: Studies structured data attribution in multimodal LLMs - whether models can point to specific rows/columns supporting an answer in tables. Finds a clear gap: while QA accuracy is moderate, attribution accuracy is much lower, near random for JSON inputs.

entry.title: Consistency-Preserving Diverse Video Generation

author.name: Xinshuang Liu, Runfa Blark Li, Truong Nguyen

entry.summary: Proposes a joint-sampling framework for flow-matching video generators that improves batch diversity across generated videos while preserving temporal consistency within each video, using lightweight latent-space objectives to avoid costly backpropagation through video decoders.

entry.title: Language and Geometry Grounded Sparse Voxel Representations for Holistic Scene Understanding

author.name: Guile Wu, David Huang, Bingbing Liu, Dongfeng Bai

entry.summary: Proposes a unified framework using language and geometry grounded sparse voxel representations that jointly models appearance, semantics, and geometry for open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding, addressing the disconnect between scene understanding and reconstruction.

entry.title: How Do We Research Human-Robot Interaction in the Age of Large Language Models? A Systematic Review

author.name: Yufeng Wang, Yuan Xu, Anastasia Nikolova, Yuxuan Wang, Jianyu Wang, Chongyang Wang, Xin Tong

entry.summary: Systematic review of 86 papers on how LLMs are reshaping human-robot interaction, examining human-centered impacts including user modeling, levels of autonomy, and socially grounded interactions. Follows PRISMA guidelines.

entry.title: Constraining Streaming Flow Models for Adapting Learned Robot Trajectory Distributions

author.name: Jieting Long, Dechuan Liu, Weidong Cai, Ian Manchester, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: Proposes CASF, a framework that augments Streaming Flow Policies with constraint-dependent metrics to reshape learned velocity fields during execution, enabling post-training enforcement of safety and task-specific constraints on robot trajectories.

entry.title: On Dwarkesh Patel’s 2026 Podcast With Elon Musk and Other Recent Elon Musk Things

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi Mowshowitz's detailed breakdown of Dwarkesh Patel's 2026 podcast with Elon Musk, covering Musk's confused views on alignment, xAI safety practices, and includes analysis of Musk's public attacks on Anthropic's Amanda Askell.

entry.title: One Agent to Guide Them All: Empowering MLLMs for Vision-and-Language Navigation via Explicit World Representation

author.name: Zerui Li, Hongpei Zheng, Fangguo Zhao, Aidan Chan, Jian Zhou, Sihao Lin, Shijie Li, Qi Wu

entry.summary: Proposes a decoupled design for MLLM-based vision-and-language navigation that separates spatial state estimation from semantic planning, introducing an interactive metric world representation for MLLMs to reason over.

entry.title: Stabilizing Test-Time Adaptation of High-Dimensional Simulation Surrogates via D-Optimal Statistics

author.name: Anna Zimmel, Paul Setinek, Gianluca Galletti, Johannes Brandstetter, Werner Zellinger

entry.summary: Proposes a test-time adaptation framework for simulation surrogates using D-optimal statistics to handle distribution shifts in high-dimensional, unstructured regression problems. Addresses the instability of existing TTA methods when applied beyond image classification.

entry.title: ZeroSyl: Simple Zero-Resource Syllable Tokenization for Spoken Language Modeling

author.name: Nicol Visser, Simon Malan, Danel Slabbert, Herman Kamper

entry.summary: Proposes ZeroSyl, a training-free method for extracting syllable boundaries from frozen WavLM models using L2 norms of intermediate layer features. Outperforms prior syllabic tokenization methods that require complex multi-stage training.

entry.title: VideoSketcher: Video Models Prior Enable Versatile Sequential Sketch Generation

author.name: Hui Ren, Yuval Alaluf, Omer Bar Tal, Alexander Schwing, Antonio Torralba, Yael Vinker

entry.summary: Presents VideoSketcher, which adapts pretrained text-to-video diffusion models for sequential sketch generation by combining LLMs for semantic planning/stroke ordering with video diffusion models for temporal rendering.

entry.title: DexEvolve: Evolutionary Optimization for Robust and Diverse Dexterous Grasp Synthesis

author.name: Ren\'e Zurbr\"ugg, Andrei Cramariuc, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: Proposes DexEvolve, a scalable generate-and-refine pipeline for synthesizing large-scale, diverse dexterous grasps using evolutionary optimization in high-fidelity simulators, moving beyond filter-only approaches to continuous improvement of grasp quality.

entry.title: Selective Perception for Robot: Task-Aware Attention in Multimodal VLA

author.name: Young-Chae Son, Jung-Woo Lee, Yoon-Ji Choi, Dae-Kwan Ko, Soo-Chul Lim

entry.summary: Proposes a dynamic information fusion framework for Vision-Language-Action models that uses a lightweight adaptive routing architecture to predict task-relevance of multiple camera views in real-time, inspired by human active perception.

entry.title: LemonadeBench: Evaluating the Economic Intuition of Large Language Models in Simple Markets

author.name: Aidan Vyas

entry.summary: Introduces LemonadeBench, a benchmark evaluating LLM economic intuition through a simulated lemonade stand business. Finds performance scales with model sophistication but reveals consistent weaknesses in inventory management.

entry.title: Indic-TunedLens: Interpreting Multilingual Models in Indian Languages

author.name: Mihir Panchal, Deeksha Varshney, Mamta, Asif Ekbal

entry.summary: Introduces Indic-TunedLens, an interpretability framework for Indian languages that learns shared affine transformations to decode intermediate LLM representations. Evaluates on 10 Indian languages.

entry.title: NeuroSymActive: Differentiable Neural-Symbolic Reasoning with Active Exploration for Knowledge Graph Question Answering

author.name: Rong Fu, Yang Li, Zeyu Zhang, Jiekai Wu, Yaohua Liu, Shuaishuai Cao, Yangchen Zeng, Yuhang Zhang, Xiaojing Du, Chuang Zhao, Kangning Cui, Simon Fong

entry.summary: Introduces NeuroSymActive, combining differentiable neural-symbolic reasoning with active, value-guided exploration for knowledge graph question answering. Aims to bridge the gap between naive graph embedding into prompts and purely symbolic approaches.

entry.title: Relative Geometry of Neural Forecasters: Linking Accuracy and Alignment in Learned Latent Geometry

author.name: Deniz Kucukahmetler, Maximilian Jean Hemmann, Julian Mosig von Aehrenfeld, Maximilian Amthor, Christian Deubel, Nico Scherf, Diaaeldin Taha

entry.summary: Studies how neural forecasters internally represent latent geometry of dynamical systems using anchor-based relative embeddings. Finds that architecture families show reproducible alignment patterns (MLPs align with MLPs, RNNs with RNNs) and alignment generally correlates with accuracy.

entry.title: Random Wavelet Features for Graph Kernel Machines

author.name: Valentin de Bassompierre, Jean-Charles Delvenne, Laurent Jacques

entry.summary: Introduces randomized spectral node embeddings whose dot products estimate graph kernels, inspired by random feature methods. Provides theoretical bounds and empirical validation for node classification and link prediction.

entry.title: Decision Quality Evaluation Framework at Pinterest

author.name: Yuqi Tian, Robert Paine, Attila Dobi, Kevin O'Sullivan, Aravindh Manickavasagam, Faisal Farooq

entry.summary: Presents Pinterest's Decision Quality Evaluation Framework for content moderation, centered on expert-curated Golden Sets and automated intelligent sampling. Evaluates both human and LLM moderation quality at scale.

entry.title: Refine Now, Query Fast: A Decoupled Refinement Paradigm for Implicit Neural Fields

author.name: Tianyu Xiong, Skylar Wurster, Han-Wei Shen

entry.summary: Proposes Decoupled Representation Refinement (DRR) for implicit neural representations, separating a deep refiner network (offline) from a fast inference embedding structure. Resolves the fidelity-speed dilemma in neural field representations.

entry.title: BindCLIP: A Unified Contrastive-Generative Representation Learning Framework for Virtual Screening

author.name: Anjie Qiao, Zhen Wang, Yaliang Li, Jiahua Rao, Yuedong Yang

entry.summary: Proposes BindCLIP, combining contrastive and generative learning for virtual screening. Adds pocket-conditioned denoising to CLIP-style pocket-ligand matching to improve sensitivity to fine-grained binding interactions.

entry.title: POP: Prior-fitted Optimizer Policies

author.name: Jan Kobiolka, Christian Frey, Gresa Shala, Arlind Kadra, Erind Bedalli, Josif Grabocka

entry.summary: POP introduces a meta-learned optimizer that predicts coordinate-wise step sizes conditioned on optimization trajectory context, trained on millions of synthetic optimization problems. It aims to eliminate sensitivity to hyperparameter choices that plague gradient-based optimizers. Evaluated on 47 benchmark optimization functions of varying dimensionality.

entry.title: Beyond Match Maximization and Fairness: Retention-Optimized Two-Sided Matching

author.name: Ren Kishimoto, Rikiya Takehi, Koichi Tanaka, Masahiro Nomura, Riku Togashi, Yoji Tomita, Yuta Saito

entry.summary: Proposes a retention-optimized objective for two-sided matching platforms (dating, recruiting), arguing that match maximization creates user imbalance and that fairness alone doesn't serve platform goals. Directly optimizes for user retention as the ultimate objective.

entry.title: Solving Parameter-Robust Avoid Problems with Unknown Feasibility using Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Oswin So, Eric Yang Yu, Songyuan Zhang, Matthew Cleaveland, Mitchell Black, Chuchu Fan

entry.summary: Addresses the mismatch between RL's expected return optimization and reachability's goal of maximizing safe sets. Proposes a robust optimization approach with unknown feasibility for safety-critical control, solving parameter-robust avoid problems.

entry.title: Loss Knows Best: Detecting Annotation Errors in Videos via Loss Trajectories

author.name: Praditha Alwis, Soumyadeep Chandra, Deepak Ravikumar, Kaushik Roy

entry.summary: Proposes detecting annotation errors in video datasets by analyzing cumulative sample loss trajectories during training. Handles both mislabeling and temporal disordering errors in phase-annotated tasks in a model-agnostic way.

entry.title: FlashMem: Supporting Modern DNN Workloads on Mobile with GPU Memory Hierarchy Optimizations

author.name: Zhihao Shu, Md Musfiqur Rahman Sanim, Hangyu Zheng, Kunxiong Zhu, Miao Yin, Gagan Agrawal, Wei Niu

entry.summary: Introduces FlashMem, a memory streaming framework for executing large DNNs on mobile GPUs that streams weights during execution rather than preloading all parameters. Enables multi-DNN workloads with reduced memory consumption.

entry.title: Making Large Language Models Speak Tulu: Structured Prompting for an Extremely Low-Resource Language

author.name: Prathamesh Devadiga, Paras Chopra

entry.summary: Investigates whether structured prompting alone can make LLMs converse in Tulu, an extremely low-resource Dravidian language with minimal digital presence. Combines grammar documentation, negative constraints, romanization, and self-play without fine-tuning.

entry.title: DependencyAI: Detecting AI Generated Text through Dependency Parsing

author.name: Sara Ahmed, Tracy Hammond

entry.summary: Introduces DependencyAI, a simple method for detecting AI-generated text using only dependency parse relation labels. Achieves competitive performance across monolingual, multi-generator, and multilingual settings with high interpretability.

entry.title: FrameRef: A Framing Dataset and Simulation Testbed for Modeling Bounded Rational Information Health

author.name: Victor De Lima, Jiqun Liu, Grace Hui Yang

entry.summary: Presents FrameRef, a large-scale dataset of 1M+ systematically reframed claims across five framing dimensions, with a simulation framework for modeling how sequential information exposure in search/recommendation systems affects users' information health.

entry.title: Training-Free Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection in 3D Brain MRI with 2D Foundation Models

author.name: Tai Le-Gia, Jaehyun Ahn

entry.summary: Introduces a training-free framework for zero-shot anomaly detection in 3D brain MRI that constructs volumetric tokens by aggregating multi-axis slices processed by 2D foundation models, addressing the gap between 2D ZSAD advances and 3D medical imaging needs.

entry.title: ToaSt: Token Channel Selection and Structured Pruning for Efficient ViT

author.name: Hyunchan Moon, Cheonjun Park, Steven L. Waslander

entry.summary: Proposes ToaSt, a decoupled framework for Vision Transformer pruning that applies head-wise structured pruning to attention modules and a novel Token Channel Selection method for Feed-Forward Networks, which constitute over 60% of FLOPs.

entry.title: RUVA: Personalized Transparent On-Device Graph Reasoning

author.name: Gabriele Conte, Alessio Mattiace, Gianni Carmosino, Potito Aghilar, Giovanni Servedio, Francesco Musicco, Vito Walter Anelli, Tommaso Di Noia, Francesco Maria Donini

entry.summary: Proposes RUVA, a 'Glass Box' personal AI architecture using a Personal Knowledge Graph for transparent, user-inspectable AI memory with precise fact redaction, contrasting with black-box RAG approaches.

entry.title: Transforming Computational Lithography with AC and AI -- Faster, More Accurate, and Energy-efficient

author.name: Saumyadip Mukhopadhyay, Kiho Yang, Kasyap Thottasserymana Vasudevan, Mounica Jyothi Divvela, Selim Dogru, Dilip Krishnamurthy, Fergo Treska, Werner Gillijns, Ryan Ryoung han Kim, Kumara Sastry, Vivek Singh

entry.summary: Reports on using accelerated computing and AI to transform computational lithography in semiconductor manufacturing, addressing the surging compute demands of angstrom-era chip fabrication.

entry.title: TokaMind: A Multi-Modal Transformer Foundation Model for Tokamak Plasma Dynamics

author.name: Tobia Boschi, Andrea Loreti, Nicola C. Amorisco, Rodrigo H. Ordonez-Hurtado, C\'ecile Rousseau, George K. Holt, Eszter Sz\'ekely, Alexander Whittle, Samuel Jackson, Adriano Agnello, Stanislas Pamela, Alessandra Pascale, Robert Akers, Juan Bernabe Moreno, Vassil Alexandrov, Mykhaylo Zayats

entry.summary: Presents TokaMind, an open-source multi-modal transformer foundation model for fusion plasma modeling, trained on heterogeneous tokamak diagnostics supporting time-series, 2D profiles, and videos.

entry.title: Knowing Isn't Understanding: Re-grounding Generative Proactivity with Epistemic and Behavioral Insight

author.name: Kirandeep Kaur, Xingda Lyu, Chirag Shah

entry.summary: Introduces the concept of 'epistemic incompleteness' in AI interactions where users lack awareness of what's missing, arguing that proactivity must go beyond anticipatory behavior to surface unknown unknowns.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning LLMs to Generate Economical and Reliable Actions for the Power Grid

author.name: Mohamad Chehade, Hao Zhu

entry.summary: Fine-tunes an LLM to generate corrective transmission switching plans for power grid emergencies (Public Safety Power Shutoffs). Uses a multi-stage pipeline with supervised fine-tuning from a DC-OPF oracle followed by direct preference optimization with AC-evaluated feedback.

entry.title: The Equalizer: Introducing Shape-Gain Decomposition in Neural Audio Codecs

author.name: Samir Sadok, Laurent Girin, Xavier Alameda-Pineda

entry.summary: Introduces shape-gain decomposition into neural audio codecs, separating signal energy from normalized structure before encoding. This classical signal processing principle improves robustness to input level variations and reduces codebook redundancy.

entry.title: Dynamic Training-Free Fusion of Subject and Style LoRAs

author.name: Qinglong Cao, Yuntian Chen, Chao Ma, Xiaokang Yang

entry.summary: Proposes dynamic training-free LoRA fusion for combining subject and style adaptations, using KL divergence-based adaptive weight selection at each layer during generation. Addresses limitations of static heuristic fusion methods.

entry.title: Lifelong Scalable Multi-Agent Realistic Testbed and A Comprehensive Study on Design Choices in Lifelong AGV Fleet Management Systems

author.name: Jingtian Yan, Yulun Zhang, Zhenting Liu, Han Zhang, He Jiang, Jingkai Chen, Stephen F. Smith, Jiaoyang Li

entry.summary: Presents LSMART, an open-source simulator for evaluating multi-agent path finding algorithms in fleet management with realistic AGV kinodynamic models. Provides comprehensive benchmarking of design choices for lifelong AGV fleet management.

entry.title: Fairness over Equality: Correcting Social Incentives in Asymmetric Sequential Social Dilemmas

author.name: Alper Demir, H\"useyin Ayd{\i}n, Kale-ab Abebe Tessera, David Abel, Stefano V. Albrecht

entry.summary: Introduces asymmetric variants of sequential social dilemma environments and proposes methods for correcting social incentives when agents face different natural incentive structures. Shows existing fairness methods struggle under asymmetry.

entry.title: Accelerated Predictive Coding Networks via Direct Kolen-Pollack Feedback Alignment

author.name: Davide Casnici, Martin Lefebvre, Justin Dauwels, Charlotte Frenkel

entry.summary: Proposes DKP-PC, combining direct feedback alignment with Kolen-Pollack algorithms to address both feedback delay and exponential decay in predictive coding networks. This makes biologically-inspired predictive coding more efficient and scalable while preserving local update properties.

entry.title: Multi-Objective Coverage via Constraint Active Search

author.name: Zakaria Shams Siam, Xuefeng Liu, Chong Liu

entry.summary: Formulates the multi-objective coverage (MOC) problem for identifying representative samples broadly covering a multi-objective space, applicable to drug discovery and materials design. Proposes a constraint-based active search approach distinct from Pareto optimization.

entry.title: Continuous-Time Piecewise-Linear Recurrent Neural Networks

author.name: Alena Br\"andle, Lukas Eisenmann, Florian G\"otz, Daniel Durstewitz

entry.summary: Extends piecewise-linear RNNs (PLRNNs) from discrete-time to continuous-time formulations for dynamical systems reconstruction. Aims to preserve the mathematical tractability of piecewise-linear design while enabling continuous-time modeling for scientific applications.

entry.title: Sparse Additive Model Pruning for Order-Based Causal Structure Learning

author.name: Kentaro Kanamori, Hirofumi Suzuki, Takuya Takagi

entry.summary: Proposes a sparse additive model-based pruning technique for order-based causal structure learning that avoids reliance on hyperparameter-sensitive hypothesis testing. Improves both computational efficiency and estimation accuracy in causal DAG discovery.

entry.title: Enabling Low-Latency Machine learning on Radiation-Hard FPGAs with hls4ml

author.name: Katya Govorkova, Julian Garcia Pardinas, Vladimir Loncar, Victoria Nguyen, Sebastian Schmitt, Marco Pizzichemi, Loris Martinazzoli, Eluned Anne Smith

entry.summary: Demonstrates first ultra-fast, radiation-hard ML application on FPGAs for high-energy physics, using hls4ml with a lightweight autoencoder for the LHCb PicoCal calorimeter. Introduces hardware-aware quantization to 10-bit weights with minimal performance loss.

entry.title: Neural Scaling Laws for Boosted Jet Tagging

author.name: Matthias Vigl, Nicole Hartman, Michael Kagan, Lukas Heinrich

entry.summary: Investigates neural scaling laws for boosted jet classification in high-energy physics using the JetClass dataset. Derives compute-optimal scaling laws and identifies effective performance limits achievable through increased compute.

entry.title: Zero-shot HOI Detection with MLLM-based Detector-agnostic Interaction Recognition

author.name: Shiyu Xuan, Dongkai Wang, Zechao Li, Jinhui Tang

entry.summary: Proposes a decoupled framework for zero-shot human-object interaction detection that separates object detection from interaction recognition, leveraging MLLMs for zero-shot interaction recognition with a deterministic generation method.

entry.title: Emergent Morphing Attack Detection in Open Multi-modal Large Language Models

author.name: Marija Ivanovska, Vitomir \v{S}truc

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic zero-shot evaluation of open-source MLLMs for face morphing attack detection, finding that LLaVA1.6-Mistral-7B achieves state-of-the-art performance without any fine-tuning, surpassing specialized MAD systems.

entry.title: RaCo: Ranking and Covariance for Practical Learned Keypoints

author.name: Abhiram Shenoi, Philipp Lindenberger, Paul-Edouard Sarlin, Marc Pollefeys

entry.summary: Introduces RaCo, a lightweight neural keypoint detector with a differentiable ranker and covariance estimator for spatial uncertainty quantification. Achieves strong rotational robustness through data augmentation alone, without expensive equivariant architectures.

entry.title: Reverse Delegated Training and Private Inference via Perfectly-Secure Quantum Homomorphic Encryption

author.name: Sergio A. Ortega, Miguel A. Martin-Delgado
